# WO-2026-08-15-01 — Codex F-1: a shop-owned list write must prove the shop belongs to the household

**This corrects a defect an external reviewer found in a LIVE system that Warwick and his mother use.
The next real shop is Tuesday. Small, surgical and provable beats clever.**

**The finding, verbatim from Codex:**

> *"`execute` validates `shop_id` only as a positive integer, resolves `household_id` separately, and
> `findOrCreateDraftList` first selects `shopping_lists where shop_id=$1`; neither that query nor
> `reclaimUnownedList` proves the shop belongs to `householdId`."*
>
> **Required correction:** *"Before reading, reclaiming, or creating a shop-owned list, require the
> supplied `shop_id` to resolve to a shop whose `household_id` equals the resolved `householdId`; fail
> closed on absence or mismatch. Provide an executed regression proving a mismatched pair writes nothing."*

**Real blast radius, so you size the fix correctly and do not over-build:** cross-**household** leakage is
**latent** — `asdair.households` holds exactly one row. Cross-**shop** misattribution within that household
is **reachable today**: four non-terminal shops are open, and a wrong or stale `shop_id` attaches an item
to the wrong shop's list. That presents exactly as the failure this module was already repaired for once —
**items Mum typed not appearing on the list that gets shopped.**

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Fail closed on mismatch.** Before any read, reclaim or create of a shop-owned list, the supplied
`shop_id` must resolve to a shop whose `household_id` equals the already-resolved `householdId`.
**On mismatch, or on a `shop_id` that resolves to no shop at all, the command REFUSES and writes NOTHING**
— no list, no reclaim, no item, no ledger row — and returns a clear, structured refusal rather than
throwing an opaque error.

**AC2 — The executed regression Codex asked for.** A dbtest against a real disposable Postgres that:
creates two shops under DIFFERENT households (and, separately, two shops under the SAME household);
issues a command pairing a `shop_id` with the wrong household; asserts **row counts are identical before
and after** across `asdair.shopping_lists`, `asdair.shopping_list_items` and the command ledger.
**Assert the counts, not merely that no exception escaped.**

**AC3 — The wrong-shop case is covered too, not just wrong-household.** With one household and two open
shops, a command naming shop B while the resolution says shop A must not write into B. **This is the case
that is reachable today** — do not let a household-only check pass while leaving it open.

**AC4 — The existing correct path is unchanged and proven so.** The reclaim-before-create repair that
Codex CONFIRMED as correct must keep working: a matching household/shop with an existing unowned list for
the same date still reclaims that list and does NOT mint a second one. **A test that fails if you break
it.** Codex confirmed this behaviour — a regression here would be worse than the defect.

**AC5 — The guard is mutation-tested.** Deliberately break the ownership check, prove the AC2/AC3 tests go
RED, restore it, prove they go GREEN. **A control is not evidence until it has been made to fail.** Report
both runs. ⚠️ Restore in a `finally` or mutate a copy — an interrupted mutation run leaves the source
mutated, which has bitten this estate before.

**AC6 — No scope creep.** No schema change, no migration, no refactor of `execute`'s unrelated commands,
no new module. If you believe a constraint is the right fix, **report it and stop** — that is a Warwick
decision, not yours or mine.

## Required evidence

**Real output pasted in the same message as the claim. Capture every exit code UNPIPED — a probe piped
into `tail` reports `tail`'s status, which has already produced one false pass in this estate.**

- The dbtest run, showing the **before/after row counts** for the mismatch cases and the executed
  subtest count. **A runner that can report zero executed tests as success is not evidence.**
- The AC5 mutation run: RED with the guard broken, GREEN with it restored, and confirmation the source was
  restored afterwards.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/control-plane/wp-d-proof` → exit code AND coverage.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/control-plane/wp-d-proof/asdairCommands.mjs services/control-plane/wp-d-proof/add-list-item.dbtest.mjs` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass
